rules.title: `ref`/`ref mut` binding adds N levels of indirection over the payload
rules.statement: A `ref`/`ref mut` pattern binding over a payload of type P binds a reference whose indirection depth = (number of Ref/MutRef layers sema wrapped on the binding type) − (number of thin-ref layers P already contributes). The binding's value is the address of the payload slot, with depth−1 intermediate slots materialized when match ergonomics flow through nested references (`&&Option<T>`). A fat-ref payload (Ref/MutRef whose repr is not a thin pointer) is excluded from this path.
rules.uncertainty: Depth>1 path is driven by match-ergonomics through nested references; exact user-visible deref count inferred from comments.

rules.title: `ref l` of a struct-typed payload binds a place reference, not a wrapped pointer
rules.statement: When `ref`/`ref mut` binds a payload field whose type is a (zoned) struct, the binding `l` denotes a reference whose value is the field's address and carries struct shape, so `l.field` projects through it directly (no extra pointer-of-pointer indirection).

rules.title: Thin `&Struct`/`&mut Struct` payload binds the loaded pointer with struct shape
rules.statement: A by-value pattern binding over a payload of type `&Struct`/`&mut Struct` (thin pointer to a (zoned) struct) binds the pointer loaded from the payload slot, carrying struct shape, so member access `q.x` projects through the referent — identical to `let r: &Struct`.

rules.title: Inline-aggregate payload binding uses the slot address as the value
rules.statement: A by-value pattern binding over an inline-aggregate payload (struct, zoned-struct, tuple, slice, closure, nested tagged enum, bare trait object) binds the payload slot's ADDRESS (no load) and carries the corresponding aggregate shape, so subsequent field/index/tuple projections work directly.

rules.title: By-value binding of a drop-bearing inline payload copies to a fresh slot
rules.statement: When an inline struct/tuple payload bound by value has a type that needs drop, the bytes are copied to a fresh local before binding; the scrutinee place's drop is suppressed (binding moves out), so later mutation of the scrutinee within the arm cannot clobber the binding.

rules.title: Scalar payload binding loads the field value into a fresh slot
rules.statement: A by-value pattern binding over a scalar (non-aggregate, non-trait, non-thin-ref-struct) payload field loads the field value from the payload slot and binds a fresh local holding that value.

rules.title: A `{ }` block restores outer bindings shadowed inside on exit
rules.statement: A lexical `{ }` block scopes its bindings: names that existed before the block and were shadowed inside revert to their outer binding when the block exits; names newly introduced inside the block do not leak.

rules.title: Destructuring-`let` field bindings leak into the enclosing scope
rules.statement: A destructuring `let` (`let Pair{a,b} = e`, `let (a,b) = e`) introduces its field bindings into the enclosing scope, including shadowing a pre-existing same-named binding; the synthetic destructure temporary does not restore scope on exit.

rules.title: Uninitialized `let mut` needs a runtime drop flag only if assigned conditionally
rules.statement: A `let mut x: T;` declared without initializer requires a runtime drop flag iff it is later assigned at a control-flow nesting depth strictly greater than its declaration depth (inside a conditional/loop/match/let-else arm). A plain `{ }` block does not increase nesting depth; variables assigned only at declaration depth use static drop placement.
rules.divergence: Implementation strategy of Rust drop-flag elaboration; observable equivalence to Rust drop semantics.

rules.title: Labeled `continue` branches to the matching enclosing loop's continue point
rules.statement: `continue 'label` transfers control to the continue point of the nearest enclosing loop whose label matches; unlabeled `continue` targets the innermost loop. Outside any loop, `continue` is a no-op.

rules.title: References and raw pointers are never droppable
rules.statement: A value of type `&T`, `&mut T`, or `*T` (raw pointer) does not require drop.

rules.title: Drop-need of dyn/slice/DST is decided by the owning bit
rules.statement: An unsized handle is droppable iff it owns its heap data: `Box<dyn Trait>` (owning trait object), `Box<[T]>` (owning slice), and owning custom-DST `Box<Foo>` require drop; their borrowed counterparts `&dyn Trait`, `&[T]`, `&Foo` do not.

rules.title: Struct/enum/tuple/array droppability is recursive plus explicit Drop
rules.statement: A (zoned) struct or enum needs drop iff it has a user `drop` method or any field/variant-payload type needs drop. A tuple needs drop iff any element needs drop. An array `[T; N]` needs drop iff `T` needs drop.

rules.title: A closure value is not auto-reported as needs-drop
rules.statement: A closure value (e.g. stored in a struct field or iterator adapter, held by pointer) is not classified as needs-drop by recursive aggregate scanning; closure drop is driven narrowly only via the owning `Box<Closure>` path.
rules.divergence: Narrows automatic Drop coverage relative to Rust for indirectly-stored closures; intentional to avoid misreading a pointer slot as a {fn,env} pair.

rules.title: Dropping a `dyn` value calls the destructor via vtable slot 0 with null guard
rules.statement: Dropping a trait-object value loads its data and vtable pointers; if data is non-null it calls vtable slot 0 (drop_in_place) on the data pointer. A null (moved-from/zeroed) data pointer skips the call.

rules.title: Dropping `Box<dyn Trait>` runs drop_in_place then frees the single heap block
rules.statement: Dropping an owning `Box<dyn Trait>` calls drop_in_place(data) via the vtable, then frees the data pointer (the single heap block holding the concrete value).

rules.title: Dropping `Rc<dyn>`/`Arc<dyn>` decrements strong and frees the RcInner at zero
rules.statement: Dropping an owning `Rc<dyn>`/`Arc<dyn>` recovers the RcInner block start as data − round_up(8, align(T)) (align read from vtable slot 2), decrements the strong count (Arc: seq-cst atomic; Rc: plain load/store) at offset 0, and only when it reaches zero calls drop_in_place(data) and frees the whole RcInner block.
rules.uncertainty: RcInner layout {strong i32, weak i32, T val} with val at round_up(8, align) and vtable layout {drop, size, align} are codegen ABI conventions inferred from comments; the dyn path frees on strong==0 without weak bookkeeping.

rules.title: A trait-object handle is a {data, vtable} fat pair
rules.statement: A trait-object value is a two-pointer fat pair: field 0 is the data pointer, field 1 is the vtable pointer; an owning smart-pointer `dyn` stores this pair inline.
